- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to counteract pessimism.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; apply dampening factor of 0.85–0.90 to peak forecasts.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >75% of 30d mean, reduce by 1–3% to align with historical volatility.
- Sentiment shifts >0.30 in 3–5 days trigger lagged correction: if sentiment turns negative, reduce forecast 1–2 days ahead; if positive, increase 1–2 days ahead.
- Model underestimates early in 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; add 0.5–1.5% to first 5–7 days if sentiment is ≤ 0.33.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.00) over 5+ days, model underperforms; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid “sentiment-induced deflation.”
